payload.issue: Two independent live dev-team dispatcher sessions each independently claimed and dispatched a QA verify-committed sub-agent for the SAME task_id (SYSREMAKE-P2-T2-SCHEMA-ADDITIONS) within seconds of each other. Both QA sub-agents ran a full independent verify-committed cycle to completion (re-running the full test matrix, re-deriving the grandfather jq query, etc.) before either discovered the collision -- the second-to-finish only found out when it tried to apply its own board write and saw orch-state.json had already moved under it.

evidence.live_incident: This session's own Review-Lane QA-Drain Head-Decoupled batch (TAKE_BUDGET=6, claimed via scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq at 2026-08-08T18:53:13Z) included SYSREMAKE-P2-T2-SCHEMA-ADDITIONS and dispatched a qa agent for it. That agent (task a9c4a76f9d3dc845a) completed a full independent APPROVED/DONE_VERIFIED review (120/120 + 8/8 + 14/14 + 29/29 + 75/75 test re-runs, grandfather-set re-derivation, mock-guard, tsc) -- then discovered on write-attempt that a DIFFERENT peer QA session had already committed the identical close-out chain (commit 9c6feb8f2 board move + 8c9a1d24a notebook/journal) moments earlier, for the same task_id and the same commit under review. The agent made zero writes itself (correctly deferred to the already-landed peer result after verifying it was sound) but the duplicate cycle itself burned 184,693 tokens / 78 tool calls / ~10.5 minutes for zero net new information -- pure waste.
evidence.root_cause: The Review-Lane QA-Drain claim script (scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq) has no task_id-level claim/lock -- it only relies on the coarse dev-team dispatch-wrapper's own outer PRE-CLAIM key (intent:dev-team:<intent>) plus the per-tick fire-election lock (cron:dev-team:<TICK>). Neither of those prevents TWO DIFFERENT live dev-team dispatcher sessions (confirmed to exist concurrently -- see project_peer_cowork_dispatcher_session_collision_20260801 for the sibling cowork-dispatcher-session finding, same root shape: a second live loop instance of the same autonomous session type) from each independently reading review[] pre-claim state, both selecting the same eligible row (status==REVIEW, next_agent=='qa', no claimed_at yet), and both dispatching a qa agent for it before either session's own orch-apply.sh CAS write against the row lands and becomes visible to the other.

payload.impact: Every Review-Lane QA-Drain batch dispatched while a second live dev-team session is running concurrently has a live per-row race window between read-eligibility and claim-write-land. Confirmed materialized once this tick (not just a theoretical residual risk as flagged in project_peer_cowork_dispatcher_session_collision_20260801's 'how to apply' section for cowork slots) -- burns a full duplicate specialist QA cycle (~10min/185K tokens observed) per collision, scales with concurrent live-session count and QA-drain batch size.
payload.requested_action: Add a task_id-level claim inside scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq's own selection+claim step (task_claim(task_id="task:<id>", ttl_seconds=<qa agent's typical runtime ceiling>) per candidate row, BEFORE stamping claimed_at/claimed_by on the board) so a second session's concurrent run of the same script sees the row already locked and skips it, rather than relying solely on the board-field CAS to serialize after the fact. Mirrors the per-slot published:<slot>:<date> dedup gate pattern that already protects cowork's guaranteed daily slots from the sibling collision shape.
payload.occurrence_note: First observed instance of this exact task_id-level QA-Drain race. Escalated immediately (not waiting for a 2nd occurrence) per the explicit standing guidance in memory project_peer_cowork_dispatcher_session_collision_20260801's how-to-apply section: 'if seen, escalate immediately as a HIGH signal_queue row to po ... given the corruption/waste potential' -- this incident is that predicted residual-risk shape materializing in a new subsystem (dev-team QA-Drain, not cowork dispatch).
